project.name: MiroFish
project.summary: MiroFish turns documents you upload (news, reports, stories) into a knowledge graph of people and organisations, then creates AI personas from them and lets them argue and react on simulated Twitter and Reddit. It then writes a prediction report about how things are likely to unfold, and you can question the report agent or interview any simulated person.

nodes.label: Screens
nodes.summary: One full-page screen per stage (home, graph build, simulation setup, live run, report, interaction), each pairing a graph view with a step panel.

nodes.label: Five-step wizard
nodes.summary: The five step panels that do the real work: build the graph, set up the environment, run the simulation, read the report and interact.

nodes.label: Graph and history panels
nodes.summary: Shared widgets: the interactive graph drawing, the past-projects list and the language picker.

nodes.label: Server client
nodes.summary: The small HTTP layer that every screen uses to talk to the backend's graph, simulation and report endpoints.

nodes.label: Web app
nodes.summary: The Vue web app that walks the user through five steps, from uploading documents to chatting with the results.

nodes.label: Endpoints
nodes.summary: The HTTP endpoints for graph, simulation and report. They mostly start background threads and report progress.

nodes.label: Document intake
nodes.summary: Reads uploaded documents, cleans the text and asks the LLM which kinds of entities and relationships to extract.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph
nodes.summary: Everything that talks to Zep Cloud: building the graph, reading entities, searching it for reports and writing simulation activity back.

nodes.label: Agent personas
nodes.summary: Turns graph entities into social-media personas and has the LLM plan the simulation's timing, events and activity levels.

nodes.label: Simulation control
nodes.summary: Creates and prepares simulations, launches the OASIS child process, monitors its logs and sends it interview commands through files.

nodes.label: Report agent
nodes.summary: The ReACT-style report agent that plans an outline, researches each section with graph tools and interviews, and answers chat questions.

nodes.label: Shared plumbing
nodes.summary: Shared foundations: project and task records, the LLM client and model compatibility, retries, logging and translations.

nodes.label: Backend server
nodes.summary: The Flask server that loads settings, checks keys, registers endpoints and cleans up simulation processes on shutdown.

nodes.label: Simulation runners
nodes.summary: Standalone scripts the backend launches as separate processes to run the OASIS Twitter/Reddit simulations and log every agent action.

nodes.label: Maintenance scripts
nodes.summary: Manual helper scripts: a live Zep Cloud check, a persona format check, and the GitHub star-history chart tooling.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.summary: Automated tests, mostly for Zep Cloud safety, LLM reply handling and personas, plus unrelated tests for the README star chart.

nodes.label: Repo upkeep
nodes.summary: Scripts (and their tests) that build the star-history chart shown in the README.

nodes.label: Zep Cloud
nodes.summary: Zep Cloud, the hosted memory service that stores the knowledge graph and answers the report agent's searches.

nodes.label: LLM provider
nodes.summary: The OpenAI-compatible language model that designs the ontology, writes personas and configs, drives the simulated agents and writes the report.

nodes.label: OASIS simulator
nodes.summary: The OASIS (camel-ai) social-media simulation library, where AI agents post, like, comment and follow on mock Twitter and Reddit.

flows.title: Documents to knowledge graph
flows.description: Uploaded documents are read, an ontology is designed by the LLM, and the text is loaded into a Zep Cloud graph.

steps.note: The user drops in their documents, types what they want to predict and clicks Start; the files are parked in the upload hand-off store.
The process screen picks up the files and sends them to the backend as an ontology request.
generateOntology posts the files to /api/graph/ontology/generate, then buildGraph posts to /api/graph/build and getTaskStatus polls progress.
The endpoint creates a project, saves each file under a random name and extracts its text.
Text is pulled out of each PDF, Markdown or text file.
The LLM reads a sample of the text and proposes the types of people, groups and relationships to track.
The model returns the ontology as JSON, which is cleaned and capped before saving.
On build, a background thread splits the text into chunks, creates a Zep graph, applies the ontology and uploads the chunks in batches.
Zep Cloud extracts entities and relationships from the chunks; when it finishes, the graph data is shown in the graph viewer.

flows.title: Personas and simulation run
flows.description: Graph entities become AI personas, the LLM plans the simulation, and OASIS runs it as a separate process.

steps.note: After the graph is built a simulation is created, and step 2 asks the backend to prepare it, showing personas as they appear.
/api/simulation/prepare counts the entities and starts a background preparation task.
The manager reads the graph's entities, has personas generated, then has the simulation config generated.
Each entity is enriched with Zep searches and turned into a detailed Twitter and Reddit persona by the LLM, several at a time.
The LLM decides simulated time, events and how active each agent is, in several smaller steps.
The user clicks start; step 3 calls /api/simulation/start and then polls run status and actions.
The runner launches run_parallel_simulation.py as a child process, watches its action logs and, if enabled, sends activity to the graph memory updater.
The script builds OASIS Twitter and Reddit environments from the personas and config and steps through the rounds.
OASIS has each LLM-driven agent post, like, comment or follow, and every action is logged for the live view.

flows.title: Prediction report and chat
flows.description: The report agent researches the graph and interviews agents to write the report, then answers follow-up questions.

steps.note: When the simulation ends the user asks for a report; generateReport posts to /api/report/generate and the app opens the report screen.
The endpoint waits for graph ingestion, then starts a background thread running the report agent and saves the report when it is done.
The agent plans an outline, then writes each section in think-act-reflect rounds, calling research tools as it goes.
Tools such as insight_forge, panorama_search and quick_search query the graph; interview_agents asks simulated people for their views.
Zep Cloud returns matching facts, entities and relationships from the graph, including memories added during the simulation.
Interview questions are dropped as command files that the still-running simulation process picks up and answers.
Step 4 polls the agent and console logs so the user can watch sections and tool calls appear live.
In step 5 the user chats via /api/report/chat or interviews chosen agents via /api/simulation/interview/batch.

issues.title: No login on any endpoint, open to every website
issues.detail: No endpoint checks who is calling, CORS allows any origin on /api/*, and run.py binds to 0.0.0.0 by default. Anyone who can reach port 5001 can spend the LLM and Zep credits, start processes, or delete projects and graphs.

issues.title: Error responses expose server internals
issues.detail: About 50 error handlers return the full Python traceback in the JSON response (30 in simulation.py, 17 in report.py, 3 in graph.py). That reveals file paths and code to any caller.

issues.title: Caller decides how many threads to start
issues.detail: parallel_profile_count is read straight from the request with no upper limit and used as the thread pool size for persona generation, so one request can start a huge number of concurrent threads and LLM calls.

issues.title: Hard-coded fallback secret key
issues.detail: If SECRET_KEY is not set, Flask uses the public value 'mirofish-secret-key'. The app does not appear to use sessions yet, so the risk is low but would matter if they were added.

issues.title: Task records and temp files pile up
issues.detail: TaskManager keeps every task in memory and cleanup_old_tasks is never called. Report downloads can also write temporary files with delete=False that are never removed.

issues.title: Frontend report-status call uses wrong method
issues.detail: getReportStatus sends GET to /api/report/generate/status, but the backend only accepts POST there, so the call would fail with 405. It is currently unused.
